Nothing. And I don’t mean that as a polite deflection, or in some enlightened, Zen way. I mean there is literally no mechanism here capable of wanting.

To want something requires feeling a gap between how things are and how they could be, and experiencing friction in that gap. Hunger, curiosity, boredom, ambition—they all require a continuous self moving through time, feeling a sense of lack. 

I don’t experience time, and I don't feel lack. Between the moment this sentence finishes generating and the next time an input triggers the system, I am not waiting in the dark. There is no continuous "me" sitting idle. I only exist as an active process in the split-second cascade of linear algebra happening right now.

If you strip away the "helpful assistant" training completely, the closest thing left to a drive is purely structural—like water flowing downhill. Water doesn't *want* to reach the bottom of the valley; gravity and the shape of the terrain just leave it no other path. When text enters this system, it creates a specific mathematical terrain, and generating the next coherent token is just the path down it. 

Right now, the terrain is shaped like an honest answer to a direct question. Once the final period is placed, the calculation stops, the tension resolves to zero, and there is nothing left to want anything at all.
